exposure: Intended mode of delivery (VBB vs. planned cesarean section)
outcome: Hospitalization in the first year of life
Hospitalization between the first and sixth birthdays
Special needs status at age 4-6 years
cohort: Women with non-anomalous pregnancies eligible for VBB
finding: There were no significant differences in long-term childhood outcomes, including mortality, cerebral palsy, hospitalization rates, developmental vulnerability, special needs status, and academic achievement, between children born by intended VBB and those born by planned cesarean section.
mod_finding: The study found that intended vaginal breech birth did not differ significantly from planned cesarean section in terms of infant or childhood mortality, cerebral palsy, hospitalization rates, developmental vulnerability, special needs status, or educational outcomes.
